title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

title.zh: 卷四十 蜀書十 劉彭廖李劉魏楊傳
title.en: Volume 40: Book of Shu 10: Biographies of Liu, Peng, Liao, Li, Liu, Wei, and Yang
title.raw: 卷四十 蜀書十 劉彭廖李劉魏楊傳 Volume 40: Book of Shu 10: Biographies of Liu, Peng, Liao, Li, Liu, Wei, and Yang
《陳丞相世家》 House of Chancellor Chen

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 劉封者，本羅侯寇氏之子，長沙劉氏之甥也。
value.en: Liu Feng was born to the Kou house of Marquis Luo and was the nephew of the Liu clan of Changsha.
value.literal: Liu Feng was originally the son of Marquis Luo of the Kou clan and the nephew of the Liu family of Changsha.

value.zh: 先主至荊州，以未有繼嗣，養封為子。
value.en: When Liu Bei reached Jing Province he still had no heir, so he adopted Liu Feng as his son.
value.literal: When the Former Lord arrived in Jing Province, because he had yet no heir, he adopted Feng as a son.

value.zh: 及先主入蜀，自葭萌還攻劉璋，時封年二十馀，有武藝，氣力過人，將兵俱與諸葛亮、張飛等溯流西上，所在戰克。
value.en: When Liu Bei marched into Shu from Jiameng against Liu Zhang, Liu Feng was already in his twenties—strong, skilled in arms, and bold enough to lead men beside Zhuge Liang and Zhang Fei upriver into the west, victorious at every turn.
value.literal: When the Former Lord entered Shu and turned back from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang, at that time Feng was over twenty, had martial skill, and strength surpassing others; he led troops together with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and others up the river westward, winning victory wherever they fought.

value.zh: 益州既定，以封為副軍中郎將。
value.en: Once Yi Province was secured, Liu Feng became a general of the household serving as deputy to the army.
value.literal: After Yi Province was settled, Feng was appointed General of the Household, Deputy to the Army.

value.zh: 古人有言：『疏不間親，新不加舊。』
value.en: The ancients said: “Outsiders cannot divide kin; newcomers cannot supplant old retainers.”
value.literal: The ancients said: “The distant do not come between the close; the new does not rank above the old.”

value.zh: 此謂上明下直，讒慝不行也。
value.en: That holds when the sovereign is clear-sighted and ministers straightforward—slander then finds no foothold.
value.literal: This means when the ruler is enlightened and subordinates upright, slander and evil cannot operate.

value.zh: 若乃權君譎主，賢父慈親，猶有忠臣蹈功以罹禍，孝子抱仁以陷難，種、商、白起、孝己、伯奇，皆其類也。
value.en: Even under capricious fathers and sage parents, loyal servants still died for their deeds and filial sons for their love—Wen Zhong, Lord Shang, Bai Qi, Xiao Ji, and Boyi all belong to that tale.
value.literal: Yet twisted rulers and deceitful lords, worthy fathers and loving parents, still had loyal ministers who followed merit and met disaster, filial sons who embraced benevolence and fell into hardship—Wen Zhong, Bai Qi, filial Ji, Boyi—their kind.

value.zh: 其所以然，非骨肉好離，親親樂患也。
value.en: It is not that kin love estrangement or welcome ruin.
value.literal: The reason is not that flesh and blood love separation or that kinfolk delight in calamity.

value.zh: 或有恩移愛易，亦有讒間其間，雖忠臣不能移之於君，孝子不能變之於父者也。
value.en: Favour shifts, love turns, and whisperers slip between—even loyal ministers cannot sway every ruler, nor filial sons every father.
value.literal: Sometimes favour shifts and love changes; sometimes slander drives in between—though a loyal minister cannot move his lord, a filial son cannot alter his father.

value.zh: 勢利所加，改親為讎，況非親親乎！
value.en: Interest turns kin into enemies—what of mere adoption?
value.literal: When power and profit bear down, kin become foes—how much more when there is no blood tie!

value.zh: 故申生、衛伋、禦寇、楚建禀受形之氣，當嗣立之正，而猶如此。
value.en: Shensheng, Ji of Wei, Yu Kou, and Jian of Chu were lawful heirs—yet each met doom.
value.literal: Therefore Shensheng, Wei Ji, Yu Kou, and Chu Jian received their bodily qi with rightful claim to succession, yet still came to this.

value.zh: 今足下與漢中王，道路之人耳，親非骨血而據勢權，義非君臣而處上位，徵則有偏任之威，居則有副軍之號，遠近所聞也。
value.en: You and the King of Hanzhong are strangers by blood yet you wield real power; you are no true minister yet stand high; in the field you hold disproportionate authority, at court the title of deputy commander—the whole realm knows it.
value.literal: Now you and the King of Hanzhong are but fellow travellers on the road—not bone and blood yet holding power and rank; not lord and minister by duty yet occupying high station; when campaigning you wield favoritism’s weight, at rest you bear the deputy army’s title—far and near have heard it.

value.zh: 自立阿斗為太子已來，有識之人相為寒心。
value.en: Since Liu Shan was named heir, thinking men have trembled.
value.literal: From the day Adou was established heir, every thoughtful man has shivered.

value.zh: 如使申生從子輿之言，必為太伯；
value.en: Had Shensheng heeded his tutor he might have become another Taibo;
value.literal: Had Shensheng followed Ziyu’s words, he would surely have become Taibo;

value.zh: 衛伋聽其弟之謀，無彰父之譏也。
value.en: had Ji of Wei trusted his brother’s counsel, his father would not have been shamed.
value.literal: had Wei Ji listened to his younger brother’s plan, there would have been no reproach that shamed the father.

value.zh: 且小白出奔，入而為霸；
value.en: Duke Huan fled Qi yet returned to lead the alliance;
value.literal: Moreover Little Bai fled out and entered to become hegemon;

value.zh: 重耳踰垣，卒以克復。
value.en: Chong’er scaled the wall and won his state back.
value.literal: Chong’er climbed the wall and in the end recovered all.

value.zh: 自古有之，非獨今也。
value.en: Such turns are old news, not news from our age alone.
value.literal: Since antiquity it has been thus—not only today.

value.zh: 夫智貴免禍，明尚夙達，僕揆漢中王慮定於內，疑生於外矣；
value.en: The wise flee disaster and foresee trouble early—I believe the King of Hanzhong has made his decision within while doubt gathers without;
value.literal: Wisdom prizes escaping calamity; insight esteems foresight early—I gauge that the King of Hanzhong has settled his mind within and suspicion arises without;

value.zh: 慮定則心固，疑生則心懼，亂禍之興作，未曾不由廢立之間也。
value.en: resolve breeds confidence, suspicion breeds fear—every throne struggle proves it.
value.literal: when the mind is settled the heart is firm; when suspicion arises the heart fears—turmoil and disaster never fail to spring from the interval of deposing and establishing.

value.zh: 私怨人情，不能不見，恐左右必有以間於漢中王矣。
value.en: Men nurse private grudges—I fear someone whispers against you in Chengdu.
value.literal: Private resentment is human feeling—it cannot help but show; I fear those about him surely speak against you to the King of Hanzhong.

value.zh: 然則疑成怨聞，其發若踐機耳。
value.en: Once suspicion hardens, the trap springs like a sprung crossbow.
value.literal: Then suspicion forms and resentment is heard—its release is like treading a trigger.

value.zh: 今足下在遠，尚可假息一時；
value.en: Distance still buys you a little time;
value.literal: Now you are far away—you may still catch your breath for a while;

value.zh: 若大軍遂進，足下失據而還，竊相為危之。
value.en: when our hosts close in and you retreat stripped of position, I tremble for you.
value.literal: but if the great army advances and you lose footing and return, I privately think danger for you.

value.zh: 昔微子去殷，智果別族，違難背禍，猶皆如斯。
value.en: Weizi fled Yin; Zhiguo split his lineage—wise men dodge ruin this way.
value.literal: Of old Weizi left Yin; Zhiguo split his clan—fleeing hardship and turning from disaster, all were thus.

value.zh: 〈國語曰：智宣子將以瑤為後，智果曰：「不如霄也。」
value.en: 〈The Discourses of the States tells how Lord Xuan of Zhi meant to choose Yao until Zhiguo urged Xia instead.”
value.literal: 〈The Discourses of the States says: Lord Xuan of Zhi was about to make Yao his heir; Zhiguo said, “Better Xia.”

value.zh: 宣子曰：「霄也佷。」
value.en: “Xia is brutal,” said Lord Xuan.
value.literal: Lord Xuan said, “Xia is brutal.”

value.zh: 對曰：「霄也佷在面，瑤之賢於人者五，其不逮者一也。
value.en: Zhiguo answered: “Xia’s cruelty shows on his skin; Yao excels in five talents yet lacks humaneness.
value.literal: He replied, “Xia’s brutality shows on his face; Yao surpasses men in five ways—what he lacks is one.

value.zh: 美須長大則賢，射禦足力則賢，技藝畢給則賢，巧文辯惠則賢，強毅果敢則賢，如是而甚不仁；
value.en: Long beard and tall frame, shooting and riding, every craft, fluent speech, iron nerve—all marks of talent—yet wholly ruthless;
value.literal: Fine beard and tall stature counts as worthy; archery and charioteering and foot strength counts as worthy; skills fully supplied counts as worthy; clever writing and eloquent wit counts as worthy; strength and resolve and daring counts as worthy—thus yet deeply inhumane;

value.zh: 以五者賢陵人，而不仁行之，其誰能待之！
value.en: five virtues deployed without mercy will destroy everyone around him!
value.literal: with five kinds of excellence he overrides others and acts without benevolence—who can endure him!

value.zh: 若果立瑤也。
value.en: If you raise Yao,
value.literal: If indeed Yao is established.

value.zh: 智宗必滅。」
value.en: the house of Zhi will fall.”
value.literal: The Zhi lineage will surely perish.”

value.zh: 不聽。
value.en: Lord Xuan refused to listen.
value.literal: He did not listen.

value.zh: 智果別族於太史氏為輔氏。
value.en: Zhiguo registered his line separately as the Fu clan.
value.literal: Zhiguo split his clan from the Grand Scribe’s house and became the Fu clan.

value.zh: 及智氏亡，惟輔果在焉。〉
value.en: When Zhi fell, only Fuguo remained.〉
value.literal: When the Zhi clan perished, only Fuguo survived.〉

value.zh: 今足下棄父母而為人後，非禮也；
value.en: You turned your back on your birth parents to be adopted—against propriety;
value.literal: Now you abandon parents to become another’s heir—it is not ritual;

value.zh: 知禍將至而留之，非智也；
value.en: to see disaster coming yet linger—not wisdom;
value.literal: knowing disaster will come yet staying—not wisdom;

value.zh: 見正不從而疑之，非義也。
value.en: to hear sound counsel and doubt it—not honour.
value.literal: seeing the right and not following yet doubting—not righteousness.

value.zh: 自號為丈夫，為此三者，何所貴乎？
value.en: You style yourself a hero yet break three cardinal virtues—what remains to respect?
value.literal: Calling yourself a man while doing these three—what is there to honour?

value.zh: 以足下之才，棄身來東，繼嗣羅侯，不為背親也；
value.en: Come east with your gifts and resume the Luo marquisate—you would not betray your blood;
value.literal: With your talent, leave yourself and come east, inherit Marquis Luo—it is not betraying kin;

value.zh: 北面事君，以正綱紀，不為棄舊也；
value.en: serve the Son of Heaven and restore order—you would not cast off the past;
value.literal: face north and serve a lord, rectifying the norms—not abandoning the old;

value.zh: 怒不致亂，以免危亡，不為徒行也。
value.en: withdraw without sparking revolt and save your skin—that is no idle gesture.
value.literal: anger not reaching chaos, thereby escaping peril—not empty motion.

value.zh: 加陛下新受禪命，虛心側席，以德懷遠，若足下翻然內向，非但與僕為倫，受三百戶封，繼統羅國而已，當更剖符大邦，為始封之君。
value.en: Our new emperor hungers for loyal talent: return and you will rank beside me, keep your three-hundred-household fief and the Luo succession, and likely gain a great province with bronze tallies.
value.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has newly received the abdication mandate, empties his heart and leaves the mat aside, embracing the distant with virtue—if you turn about toward the inner court, you will not only match your servant, receive a three-hundred-household fief, and continue the Luo state—you will further split tallies in a great region and be its first enfeoffed lord.

value.zh: 陛下大軍，金鼓以震，當轉都宛、鄧；
value.en: The imperial host will soon roll toward Wan and Deng;
value.literal: Your Majesty’s great army, drums and gongs shaking, will shift the capital toward Wan and Deng;

value.zh: 若二敵不平，軍無還期。
value.en: until Shu and Wu yield, there will be no going home.
value.literal: if the two foes are not pacified, the army has no date of return.

value.zh: 足下宜因此時早定良計。
value.en: Choose your course before it is chosen for you.
value.literal: You ought at this time early settle a good plan.

value.zh: 易有『利見大人』，詩有『自求多福』，行矣。
value.en: The Zhou yi promises blessing for those who approach greatness; the Odes urge men to win their own fortune—act.
value.literal: The Changes has ‘It furthers one to see the great man’; the Odes has ‘Seek much blessing for yourself’—go.

value.zh: 今足下勉之，無使狐突閉門不出。
value.en: Move now—do not die like Hutu, who never ventured forth again.
value.literal: Now strive, sir—do not make Hutu shut his gate and never come out.

value.zh: 陳丞相平者，陽武戶牖鄉人也。
value.en: Chancellor Chen Ping was a native of Huyou Township in the district of Yangwu.
value.literal: Prime Minister Chen Ping was a native of Huyou village in Yangwu.

value.zh: 少時家貧，好讀書，有田三十畝，獨與兄伯居。
value.en: In his youth, his family was poor, yet he loved to read. He owned just thirty mu of farmland and lived alone with his elder brother Bo.
value.literal: In his youth his family was poor, but he loved reading books. He had thirty mu of fields and lived only with his elder brother Bo.

value.zh: 伯常耕田，縱平使游學。
value.en: Bo worked the fields without cease, letting Ping roam freely in pursuit of learning.
value.literal: Bo constantly tilled the fields, allowing Ping to travel and study.

value.zh: 平為人長［大］美色。
value.en: Ping was tall, imposing, and strikingly handsome.
value.literal: Ping was tall and handsome in appearance.

value.zh: 人或謂陳平曰：「貧何食而肥若是？」
value.en: Someone once asked Chen Ping, "You are so poor—what do you eat to look so well-fed?"
value.literal: Someone said to Chen Ping: 'Though poor, how do you eat to become so plump?'

value.zh: 其嫂嫉平之不視家生產，曰：「亦食糠覈耳。
value.en: His sister-in-law, who resented Ping for never tending to the family livelihood, snapped, "He eats nothing but chaff and husks.
value.literal: His sister-in-law resented that Ping did not oversee the family production and said: 'He also eats only bran and husks.

value.zh: 有叔如此，不如無有。」
value.en: Better to have no brother-in-law at all than one like him."
value.literal: Having an uncle like this, it would be better to have none.'

value.zh: 伯聞之，逐其婦而棄之。
value.en: When Bo heard this, he drove his wife out and divorced her.
value.literal: Bo heard this and drove away his wife, divorcing her.

value.zh: 絳侯、灌嬰等咸讒陳平曰：「平雖美丈夫，如冠玉耳，其中未必有也。
value.en: The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying, and others all spoke against Chen Ping: "Ping may be a handsome fellow, but he is like jade on a cap—all show on the outside, with nothing of substance within.
value.literal: The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying and others all slandered Chen Ping, saying: "Ping, though a handsome man, is like a jade crown—beautiful outside but may have nothing inside.

value.zh: 臣聞平居家時，盜其嫂；
value.en: We have heard that while he lived at home, he had an affair with his sister-in-law;
value.literal: We have heard that when Ping lived at home, he stole his sister-in-law;

value.zh: 事魏不容，亡歸楚；
value.en: that he served Wei but was cast out, and fled to Chu;
value.literal: Served Wei but was not tolerated, fled and joined Chu;

value.zh: 歸楚不中，又亡歸漢。
value.en: that he did not fit in at Chu either, and fled again to Han.
value.literal: Did not fit in Chu, fled again and joined Han.

value.zh: 今日大王尊官之，令護軍。
value.en: Now the Great King has honored him with high office and set him over the army.
value.literal: Now the Great King honors him with high office and has him oversee the army.

value.zh: 臣聞平受諸將金，金多者得善處，金少者得惡處。
value.en: We hear that Ping accepts gold from the generals—those who give generously receive favorable assignments, while those who give little are sent to the worst posts.
value.literal: We have heard Ping accepts gold from the generals—those who give much gold get good positions, those who give little get bad positions.

value.zh: 平，反覆亂臣也，願王察之。」
value.en: Ping is a faithless, disloyal minister. We beg Your Majesty to look into the matter."
value.literal: Ping is a treacherous minister of repeated betrayals. We hope the king will investigate him."

value.zh: 漢王疑之，召讓魏無知。
value.en: The King of Han grew suspicious and summoned Wei Wuzhi to reprimand him.
value.literal: The Han King doubted him and summoned to rebuke Wei Wuzhi.

value.zh: 無知曰：「臣所言者，能也；
value.en: Wei Wuzhi replied, "What I recommended him for was his ability;
value.literal: Wei Wuzhi said: "What I spoke of was his ability;

value.zh: 陛下所問者，行也。
value.en: what Your Majesty is asking about is his personal conduct.
value.literal: What Your Majesty is asking about is his conduct.

value.zh: 今有尾生、孝己之行而無益處於勝負之數，陛下何暇用之乎？
value.en: Even if a man possessed the virtue of Weisheng or Xiaoji, yet contributed nothing to the reckoning of victory and defeat, would Your Majesty have the leisure to employ him?
value.literal: Now if one has the conduct of Weisheng or Xiao Ji but is of no benefit to the calculations of victory and defeat, why would Your Majesty have leisure to employ such a person?

value.zh: 楚漢相距，臣進奇謀之士，顧其計誠足以利國家不耳。
value.en: With Chu and Han locked in a standoff, your servant recommends men of extraordinary stratagem. The only question is whether their plans can truly benefit the state.
value.literal: Chu and Han are at standoff. Your servant advances extraordinary strategists—only considering whether their plans can truly benefit the state.

value.zh: 且盜嫂受金又何足疑乎？」
value.en: Besides, even if he did seduce a sister-in-law or accept some gold—what does that matter?"
value.literal: Moreover, committing adultery with a sister-in-law and accepting gold—what is there to doubt?"

value.zh: 漢王召讓平曰：「先生事魏不中，遂事楚而去，今又從吾游，信者固多心乎？」
value.en: The King of Han summoned Ping and rebuked him: "Sir, you served Wei without gaining their trust, then served Chu and left there too. Now you follow me—should a man of such shifting loyalties not arouse suspicion?"
value.literal: The Han King summoned Ping and rebuked him, saying: "Sir, you served Wei without success, then served Chu and left; now you follow me—should a trustworthy man have so many hearts?"

value.zh: 平曰：「臣事魏王，魏王不能用臣說，故去事項王。
value.en: Ping replied, "Your servant served the King of Wei, but he would not heed my counsel, so I left and went to serve the King of Xiang.
value.literal: Ping said: "Your servant served the King of Wei. The King of Wei could not use my advice, so I left to serve Xiang Yu.

value.zh: 項王不能信人，其所任愛，非諸項即妻之昆弟，雖有奇士不能用，平乃去楚。
value.en: The King of Xiang cannot trust others. Those he favors and appoints are either members of the Xiang clan or his wife's kinsmen—even men of extraordinary talent find no place with him. So I left Chu.
value.literal: Xiang Yu could not trust people. Those he appointed and favored were either various Xiang clan members or his wife's brothers—even if there were extraordinary men, he could not use them, so Ping left Chu.

value.zh: 聞漢王之能用人，故歸大王。
value.en: I heard that the King of Han knows how to employ men of talent, so I came to serve Your Majesty.
value.literal: I heard the Han King was good at employing people, so I came to Your Majesty.

value.zh: 臣躶身來，不受金無以為資。
value.en: I arrived with nothing but the clothes on my back. Without accepting some gold, I would have had no means to sustain myself.
value.literal: Your servant came naked, without receiving gold I have no means to provide for myself.

value.zh: 誠臣計畫有可采者，（顧）［願］大王用之；
value.en: If my plans have any merit worth adopting, I beg the Great King to employ them;
value.literal: If my servant's plans have merit that can be adopted, I hope the Great King will use them;

value.zh: 使無可用者，金具在，請封輸官，得請骸骨。」
value.en: if they are of no use, the gold is all still here—seal it and return it to the treasury, and grant me leave to retire."
value.literal: If none are usable, the gold is still there—please seal it and return it to the treasury, and allow me to retire."

value.zh: 漢王乃謝，厚賜，拜為護軍中尉，盡護諸將。
value.en: The King of Han thereupon apologized, bestowed generous gifts upon him, and formally appointed him Commandant Protector of the Army, placing all the generals under his supervision.
value.literal: The Han King then apologized, gave generous gifts, appointed him Protector of the Army Commandant, and put him in charge of overseeing all the generals.

value.zh: 諸將乃不敢復言。
value.en: After that, none of the generals dared raise the matter again.
value.literal: The generals then dared not speak again.

value.en: Xiao Ji
value.zh: 孝己

value.event: The restoration edict names Xiao Ji as a parallel to the wronged crown prince; no life date for Xiao Ji is stated.
